stem: Which of the following systems of equations has infinitely many solutions?
solution: A system has infinitely many solutions when the two equations describe the same line, that is, when one equation is a multiple of the other.
In every other choice the second equation is not a multiple of the first: the lines are parallel (no solution) or cross once.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Multiplying the first equation by \(-3\) gives \(-6x + 3y = -12\), not \(12\); these lines are parallel, so the system has no solution.
explanation.B: Correct. Multiplying \(2x - y = 4\) by \(-3\) gives \(-6x + 3y = -12\), so both equations describe the same line.
explanation.C: Incorrect. These lines have slopes \(2\) and \(-2\), so they intersect in exactly one point.
explanation.D: Incorrect. These lines have slopes \(2\) and \(-2\), so they intersect in exactly one point, \((2, 0)\).

verify:
eqs = lambda s: [value(p.split('=')[0]) - value(p.split('=')[1]) for p in s.split(' and ')]
x, y = symbols('x y')
inf = [k for k in choices if len(linsolve(eqs(choices[k]), [x, y]).free_symbols) > 0]
assert inf == [answer]
